### R

```{r}
#| label: newton-quadratic-3d-r
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| eval: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Surface plot of f(x) = (x1^2 + 3 x2^2) / 2 for x1 from -4 to 4 and x2
#|   from -2 to 2. The surface is a bowl with its lowest point at the origin,
#|   rising more steeply along x2 than along x1. A vermilion point marks the
#|   start (3, 1) on the bowl's side and a black point marks the minimizer
#|   at the origin.
nq_x1_sf <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 61)
nq_x2_sf <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = 61)
nq_grid_sf <- tidyr::expand_grid(x1 = nq_x1_sf, x2 = nq_x2_sf)
nq_value_sf <- (nq_grid_sf$x1^2 + 3 * nq_grid_sf$x2^2) / 2
nq_n2_sf <- length(nq_x2_sf)
nq_z_sf <- matrix(nq_value_sf, nrow = nq_n2_sf)
nq_start_sf <- tibble::tibble(x1 = 3, x2 = 1, z = 6)
nq_min_sf <- tibble::tibble(x1 = 0, x2 = 0, z = 0)
nq_red_sf <- list(color = "#D55E00", size = 5)
nq_black_sf <- list(color = "#000000", size = 5)
nq_stops_sf <- c(0, 1)
nq_cols_sf <- c("#CCE0F0", "#0072B2")
nq_scale_sf <- list(nq_stops_sf, nq_cols_sf)
nq_eye_sf <- list(x = 1.6, y = -1.6, z = 0.9)
nq_camera_sf <- list(eye = nq_eye_sf)
nq_xaxis_sf <- list(title = "x1")
nq_yaxis_sf <- list(title = "x2")
nq_zaxis_sf <- list(title = "f(x)")
nq_scene_sf <- list(
  xaxis = nq_xaxis_sf,
  yaxis = nq_yaxis_sf,
  zaxis = nq_zaxis_sf,
  camera = nq_camera_sf
)
nq_legend_sf <- list(orientation = "h")
plotly::plot_ly() |>
  plotly::add_surface(
    x = nq_x1_sf,
    y = nq_x2_sf,
    z = nq_z_sf,
    colorscale = nq_scale_sf,
    showscale = FALSE,
    opacity = 0.8
  ) |>
  plotly::add_trace(
    data = nq_start_sf,
    x = ~x1,
    y = ~x2,
    z = ~z,
    type = "scatter3d",
    mode = "markers",
    marker = nq_red_sf,
    name = "start"
  ) |>
  plotly::add_trace(
    data = nq_min_sf,
    x = ~x1,
    y = ~x2,
    z = ~z,
    type = "scatter3d",
    mode = "markers",
    marker = nq_black_sf,
    name = "minimizer"
  ) |>
  plotly::layout(scene = nq_scene_sf, legend = nq_legend_sf)
```

```{r}
#| eval: !expr isFALSE(knitr::is_html_output())
#| results: asis

  "*(This 3D surface is interactive; see the HTML or slide version",

)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: newton-quadratic-3d-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Surface plot of f(x) = (x1^2 + 3 x2^2) / 2 for x1 from -4 to 4 and x2
#|   from -2 to 2. The surface is a bowl with its lowest point at the origin,
#|   rising more steeply along x2 than along x1. A vermilion point marks the
#|   start (3, 1) on the bowl's side and a black point marks the minimizer
#|   at the origin.
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 6
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

nq_x1_3d, nq_x2_3d = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(-4, 4, 61),
                                 np.linspace(-2, 2, 61))
nq_z_3d = (nq_x1_3d**2 + 3 * nq_x2_3d**2) / 2
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4.5))
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection="3d")
ax.plot_surface(nq_x1_3d, nq_x2_3d, nq_z_3d, color="#0072B2", alpha=0.6)
ax.scatter([3], [1], [6], color="#D55E00", label="start")
ax.scatter([0], [0], [0], color="black", label="minimizer")
ax.set_xlabel("x1")
ax.set_ylabel("x2")
ax.set_zlabel("f(x)")
ax.legend(loc="upper right")
plt.show();
```

:::

The [graph](functions.qmd#def-graph) of $f$ in @exm-newton-quadratic is a bowl
whose lowest point is the origin.

:::
